title: Invoice and payment
summary: An invoice has two fields that move. Its status is draft, then issued, and an issued invoice never changes again except its payment_status: pending, failed, paid, paid_outside or credited. There is no void state; corrections are credit notes. The bottom half is how a card payment reaches Stripe and how Stripe's events come back.

boxes.label: The month's records
boxes.detail: computeLines charges each UTC day to the plan assignment in force at 00:00: consecutive days of one assignment make one line with the base price prorated by day, and trial and trial_unpaid days are lines at 0. Overage from billing_overage is priced per assignment, alerts one by one and data points by whole blocks, and at 0 under a trial. A month with no plan cannot be invoiced.

boxes.label: No invoice yet
boxes.detail: billing:draft-invoices runs daily at 02:10 and drafts each ended month for every account that had a plan in it, once the runtime's usage watermark has reached the month's end. Until then the account waits; after BILLING_INVOICE_WAIT_DAYS (3) the admin list marks it overdue and an administrator can draft anyway, which marks the draft usage_incomplete.

boxes.label: Draft
boxes.detail: A draft can be recalculated from the records at any time, keeping the administrator's adjustments, and can be deleted with its account. Owners never see it: a draft answers 404. A draft of the running month is a preview. Issuing is refused with 409 until the month has ended, while a usage_incomplete draft has not been recalculated after its usage became final, or when its lines no longer match the records.

boxes.label: Issued, pending
boxes.detail: Issuing, in one transaction: the next number from a locked counter row, so there are no gaps; snapshots of the operator's and the account's details and the tax rate; the account's credit applied after tax; due in BILLING_INVOICE_DUE_DAYS (14). From then on the model refuses any write except payment_status. The billing contact and every owner get the PDF by email. An invoice with nothing due is paid at once.

boxes.label: Paid
boxes.detail: What is still owed is the amount due less the credit notes' applied parts and the payments that succeeded. Once nothing is owed the invoice is paid, its open Checkout pages are expired and the account's past due flag is refreshed. A payment for more than was owed keeps the rest as account credit for the next invoice.

boxes.label: Paid outside
boxes.detail: An administrator records a payment made another way, up to what is still owed, with a note. It works whether or not card payments are on. When that payment is the one that settles the invoice, it reads paid_outside. Owners get a receipt as for any payment.

boxes.label: Failed
boxes.detail: A failed card or Checkout payment marks an unsettled invoice failed and emails the owners the card issuer's reason. Nothing is restricted. Once the due date has passed the account is flagged past_due_since until no invoice is overdue. A failed invoice is settled by a later payment, a payment recorded by hand or a credit note, like a pending one.

boxes.label: Credited
boxes.detail: A credit note has its own number sequence and an amount up to the part of the invoice not yet credited. It takes what it can off what is still owed; the rest becomes account credit for the next invoice. When it leaves nothing owed the invoice reads credited. The invoice's own figures never change.

boxes.label: ChargeInvoice
boxes.sub: Attempt 1, 2 on due date, 3 at +7 days
boxes.detail: Queued at issue when payments are on, the account has a card and something is due; billing:payment-reminders (daily at 09:00) queues attempts 2 and 3 with the owners' reminders, within 30 days of the due date. It records a pending payment first, then asks Stripe for an off-session PaymentIntent with the idempotency key invoice:{uuid}:{attempt}. An amount under BILLING_CARD_MINIMUM is never sent.

boxes.label: Stripe
boxes.detail: A decline answers at once and fails the payment. A request Stripe refuses outright charged nothing, so the payment fails with Stripe's reason. A timeout, a rate limit or Stripe's own error leaves the payment pending: the job retries with the same key, and the pending payment blocks the next attempt and the Pay page until an event arrives or an administrator checks with Stripe. Owners can also pay on a Checkout page, which expires after 30 minutes.

boxes.label: StripeEvents
boxes.detail: POST /api/stripe/webhook verifies the signature (403 otherwise) and answers 404 while payments are off. Four events are handled: checkout.session.completed, payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed and payment_method.detached. The event id goes into billing_provider_events first and is acted on only when new. A payment only moves forward: pending to failed or succeeded, failed to succeeded.

steps.text: After a month ends, the daily job waits until the runtime has reported usage to the month's end, then drafts an invoice for each account that had a plan in it.
The lines come from the records: paid days prorated from the base price, trial days at 0, and overage priced per plan assignment.
An administrator reviews the draft, can recalculate it and can add a credit or a charge as an adjustment.
Issuing gives it the next number, fixes tax and details, applies the account's credit and sets the due date. From here only payment_status changes.
With card payments on and a saved card, issuing queues the first charge. A pending payment is recorded before Stripe is asked.
The charge is an off-session PaymentIntent with one idempotency key per attempt, so a retried job charges once.
Stripe's signed events come back to the webhook. Each event id is stored first and acted on once.
A succeeded payment settles the invoice once nothing is owed, and the owners get a receipt.
A failed payment marks the invoice failed and emails the owners the reason.

On the due date and seven days after, owners are reminded and the saved card is charged again; an owner can also pay on Stripe's page. Past the due date the account reads past due, and nothing is restricted.
An administrator can record a payment made another way, which is the only way to settle while card payments are off.
A credit note that leaves nothing owed makes the invoice credited; any rest becomes account credit for the next invoice.
